transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I really hope I'm not taking up time from someone who needs it more, but... well, my wife really wanted me to come speak with you. 

It's, um, it's about work. I do environmental modeling, and... I don't want to sound unreasonable, I really don't. I know how this might sound. But I'm pretty sure the people on our current contract have been tracking my revisions. And, well, I think they're planting errors in the datasets. Just to make it look like I can't lead the work anymore. 

My wife and the junior analysts, they're very supportive, and they keep telling me it's just version-control mistakes, you know, normal software glitches. And I try to listen to them, I really do. But I just... I feel like it's deliberate. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it alright. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you believe that certain people are specifically targeting you or acting against you in a way that others don't seem to notice?

Well, yes... I suppose that is exactly what I mean. Like I was just saying about the people on our contract. I really hate to say they are targeting me, because I know how dramatic that sounds, and I promise I'm usually very easy to work with. I don't want to cause any trouble or point fingers. But... yes, I do feel like they are specifically acting against me. 

Tracking my revisions, slipping those errors into the datasets... it feels very deliberate, just to make it look like I can't lead the project anymore. And it is exactly like you said, the others really don't seem to notice it at all. Like I mentioned, my wife and the junior analysts just keep telling me it is only version-control mistakes or normal software glitches. They are wonderful people, they really are, and I know they are just trying to help, but they just don't see the pattern I'm seeing. 

I hope it is alright that I'm being so frank about this. I know it must sound a bit strange, but I just want to be a good patient and give you the full picture. Did I answer your question okay?
Have you ever experienced things that others around you don’t seem to experience — like hearing voices, seeing things that aren’t there, or feeling sensations that don’t have a clear cause?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. I really want to be clear about that, Doctor. I know sometimes when people talk about... well, feeling targeted, it can sound like they might be imagining things. But I promise you, I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. 

I'm just a normal guy, really. I just do my environmental modeling, look at the math, look at the data... it's all very grounded in reality. I don't have any strange sensations or anything. It's just this very specific situation at work with the datasets. 

I hope that reassures you? I really don't want you to think I'm... well, you know, completely losing my grip or anything like that. I'm trying very hard to be objective about all this. Does that make sense?
Doctor: Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs that other people might find strange or hard to believe, even if they weren’t about being targeted at work?

No, no, I really don't think so. I try to stay pretty grounded, you know? Like I said, I just focus on the math and the modeling. I don't really have any... well, unusual ideas about how the world works or anything like that. 

I really hope I'm not coming across as someone who just makes things up. I try to be very reasonable. I mean, aside from this whole mess with the contract and the datasets, I think most people would say I'm pretty practical. I just want to do my job well and not cause a fuss. 

I haven't had any other strange beliefs or anything like that, I promise. Is that... is that the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
How certain are you that the people on your contract are deliberately targeting you and planting errors in the datasets, despite others not noticing it?

Well, I... I suppose I'm very certain. I mean, I don't want to sound stubborn or like I won't listen to reason. I know my wife and the junior analysts think it's just version-control mistakes, and I respect their opinions so much. They're smart people. But... when I really look at the data, the way the errors are planted right after my revisions... it just feels too precise to be an accident. 

I really am pretty sure they're doing it to make it look like I can't lead the work anymore. I hate saying that out loud because I know it sounds like I'm just pointing fingers, and I promise I'm usually the first one to take the blame if I mess up a calculation. But this... this just feels different. 

I hope it's okay that I'm sticking to my guns on this one? I don't want to seem difficult or uncooperative. I just... I really believe this is what's happening, even if the others don't see it yet. Am I explaining that alright?
Even though others have explained that these might just be software glitches or version-control mistakes, do you still feel certain that someone is intentionally planting these errors?

I... yes. Yes, I do. I mean, I really don't want to come across as someone who ignores good advice. My wife is brilliant, and the junior analysts, they're good kids, they really are. When they say it's just software glitches, I... I listen to them. I really try to take that in. 

But when I sit down and look at the actual datasets... the way the errors appear right after I've tracked my revisions... it's just... it's too deliberate. I'm pretty sure they're tracking exactly what I do and planting those mistakes to make me look incompetent. To make it look like I shouldn't be leading the work anymore. 

I know it probably sounds terrible of me to say that, and I hate thinking poorly of my colleagues. I really do. I just... I can't shake the feeling that it's intentional, despite what everyone else says. I hope you don't think less of me for not just accepting the version-control explanation? I just have to be honest about what I'm seeing in the math. Is it... is it okay that I still feel this way, even after they've tried to explain it away?

Even though your wife and the junior analysts have given you alternative explanations and seem to believe the errors are accidental, do you still feel completely convinced that these are deliberate acts against you?

I know I keep saying the same thing, and I'm so sorry if I'm frustrating you or not giving you the answer you're looking for. I really want to be helpful, I do. But... yes. I am completely convinced. 

I know my wife and the junior analysts mean well when they tell me it's just version-control mistakes. They're wonderful people. But I'm the one who has been leading this environmental modeling contract, and when I look at the math... I just know they've been tracking my revisions and planting those errors. They're doing it to make it look like I can't lead the work anymore. 

I know that sounds awful, and I hate being the kind of person who won't just accept a simple explanation. I really pride myself on being reasonable and easy to work with. But I just can't ignore what's right there in the datasets, even when everyone else tells me I'm wrong. I hope you can understand where I'm coming from? I'm really trying my best to be completely open with you about this, even though it's embarrassing to admit. Are we... are we okay? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
